architecture.mechanism: Clearance between the flat-faced follower and its guides introduces non-linear impact dynamics that amplify contact stress on the cam-follower interface.
architecture.intervention: Use the paper's non-linear dynamic simulation methodology to quantify existing guide clearances in the folding station, then machine or shim the follower guides to minimize clearance to the lowest value that prevents binding at 420 cycles per minute, thereby reducing impact-induced peak Hertzian stresses without altering the cam profile or the 16 mm follower diameter class.
architecture.expected_effect: Reducing guide clearance suppresses non-linear impact forces transmitted through the follower stem to the flat face, lowering peak cyclic contact stress below the rolling-contact fatigue threshold of the follower material and extending service life beyond 9 weeks without requiring weekly maintenance.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument a test follower with a triaxial accelerometer on the stem and run the station at 420 cycles per minute; measure peak impact acceleration amplitudes before and after guide clearance reduction. If peak accelerations do not decrease by at least 30 percent and spalling still occurs within 9 weeks on food-contact inspection, the intervention is falsified.
